stances.claim: Aquino had the doctrinal conviction and the legal team but not the military assets to enforce PH WPS rights -- and refused to face China alone bilaterally, opting for the legal arbitration he could win.

Carpio, who backstopped the PH legal panel, has outlined four proactive measures short of war -- suing China in UNCLOS-ratifying states, asking the Seabed Authority to suspend Chinese exploration permits, asking the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf to suspend China's ECS application, and actively patrolling the WPS while invoking the PH-US Mutual Defense Treaty if attacked.
stances.rhetorical_move: enumerated-toolkit attributed to a credentialed insider

stances.claim: Duterte's friendship strategy has produced tangible benefits -- Filipino fisherfolk allowed at Scarborough, no Chinese construction there, and no Chinese assertion of Scarborough's 12-NM territorial sea -- and these constitute a 'major giveaway' from China because they broke the nine-dash-line plan of three SCS bases.

Despite his friendly stance, Duterte has lately used sterner measures -- diplomatic protests over the Recto Bank ramming, the Pag-asa swarming, the Sibuto Strait passage -- and has publicly promised to raise the arbitral award and code of conduct with Xi in Beijing, showing the strategy is taking firmer form.

We are now united in our goal -- protecting WPS rights -- and are 'getting united also in the methods.' On international interests, Filipinos should 'loudly disagree on domestic policies' but 'silently unite as one people' against foreign claimants.
stances.rhetorical_move: national-unity exhortation with explicit domestic/foreign distinction

notable_anecdotes: The Chinese seizure timeline as a single forced inventory: Paracels 1974, Fiery Cross 1987, Johnson South 1988, Subi 1988, Mischief 1995 -- 'did not cause much concern to ordinary Filipinos at the time' -- until Scarborough 2012 'rang deafening alarm bells' for Aquino. The escalating geographic proximity is itself the argument.

Carpio's four proposed measures cited not from interview but specifically from 'page 216 of his seminal book' -- the kind of precise sourcing that CJ used as both attribution and oblique recommendation of the book to readers.

The 'major giveaway' framing -- China's restraint at Scarborough (no construction, no 12-NM territorial-sea assertion) reinterpreted not as random goodwill but as breaking the nine-dash-line three-base plan (Paracels done, Spratlys done, Scarborough not done) -- a structural read that turns a quiet absence into a doctrinal victory.
The 'firing' of diplomatic protests in scare quotes -- gently acknowledging the slang while listing the three concrete incidents being protested.
The closing chiastic doublet: 'loudly disagree on domestic policies... silently unite as one people in protecting our international interests' -- the column's rhetorical apex.
target_audience: Filipino voters watching the Aquino-vs-Duterte strategy debate
FLP donors interested in legacy WPS coverage

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban traces the Chinese seizures across the SCS -- Paracels (1974), Fiery Cross (1987), Johnson South and Subi (1988), Mischief (1995) -- that built up to the 2012 Scarborough seizure that 'rang deafening alarm bells' for Aquino III. He explains Aquino's choice of UNCLOS arbitration as the rational response of a leader with the legal conviction but not the military assets to confront China bilaterally, and recounts the aggressive enforcement options Carpio outlined on page 216 of his book: sue China in UNCLOS-ratifying states to attach extraction assets, ask the International Seabed Authority to suspend Chinese permits, petition the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf to suspend China's East China Sea application, and patrol the WPS while invoking the PH-US Mutual Defense Treaty if attacked. He then defends Duterte's friendship-first approach by accounting for specific concessions secured -- Filipino fishing at Scarborough, no Chinese construction there, no assertion of Scarborough's 12-NM territorial sea -- and reframes that restraint as a 'major giveaway' that broke the nine-dash-line plan of three SCS bases. The recent diplomatic protests over Recto Bank, the Pag-asa 'swarming,' and the Sibuto Strait passage show, he argues, that Duterte is taking firmer measures when needed. His closing exhortation distills the column: Filipinos can 'loudly disagree on domestic policies' but should 'silently unite as one people in protecting our international interests.'
